items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: The 12th of November I recorded under my own name with Stephane Grappelli, Joseph Reinhardt on guitar, Wilson Meyers and Ted Fields, drums.

ctx.x: Some of those brothels were pretty remarkable places. Some of them were very exclusive. They had different rooms. Each one representing a different culture. If you thought you wanted to be out in the desert, they had a room with a tent in it. This was an amazing thing in those days, and I think had a certain value as far as crime was concerned. It was certainly attractive to anyone from the States, and particularly for the Blacks who were unable to mix at home. They had a chance to experience the opposite side of…

I renewed my acquaintance with Willy Lewis whom I had met in 1933, in Monte-Carlo with June Cole and Ted Fields. Willy was leading an orchestra in a high society club called "Chez Florence", on rue Blanche and not far from the bar and hotel de Lizieux where many of the American negro musicians would congregate when they had finished their nights work.

But the surprise of surprises was meeting Benny Carter one night at the Lizieux's bar a few nights after I had arrived in Paris. As I had been in Cincinnati a few months before coming to France and the way I was obliged to pass through the Apple, I had not picked up on the latest events, so I had no idea that Benny was in Paris until I saw him this night.
